constraints._note: Creator constraints set at intake 2026-08-07. fin-facts and fin-audit both enforce these; they are not suggestions.
constraints.no_return_promise: Never promise or imply a return rate. The corpus number is arithmetic FROM a stated assumption, never a forecast. Say the assumption out loud in the VO the first time a number depends on it.
constraints.withdrawal_rate_on_screen: Every corpus figure must carry its assumed withdrawal/return rate ON SCREEN in the same frame as the number. A number without its assumption visible is a fabricated promise.
constraints.no_unsourced_retire_early: No 'retire early', 'quit your job', or financial-freedom-by-age claim that is not sourced and dated in facts-staging.md.
constraints.hi_currency_framing: ₹ cut: SIP/SWP vocabulary, financial freedom / passive income framing. The word 'dividend' (and its Hindi/Devanagari transliterations) must not appear in the hi script, on-screen text, title, or tags.
constraints.market_rewrite_not_translation: The en cut is a US rewrite (US vehicles, US numbers, Brian voice), not a translation of the hi cut — see vault/knowledge/us-english-script-style.md.
constraints.derived_income_carries_assumption: EXTENDED 2026-08-07 during ch2 review. `withdrawal_rate_on_screen` was written about CORPUS figures, so the build assert let s17's `WHAT ₹2,500 BUYS` through bare — correctly, by the letter. But ₹2,500/month is the corpus's OUTPUT at 3.0%, i.e. the promise the video actually makes, and `no_return_promise` says a number without its assumption visible is a fabricated promise. So a DERIVED INCOME figure carries the rate in frame or an explicit ILLUSTRATIVE marker, same as a corpus. Every rung has a 'what X buys' beat, so this lives in the build assert, not in per-chapter review.
